claim: In the two-marked-vertex coined discrete-time walk on a star with \(N\ge2\) external vertices analyzed by Štefaňák and Skoupý, let \(s\) and \(r\) be the marked sender and receiver leaves and let \(\omega=\arccos((N-4)/N)\). Their exact formula gives the sender-to-receiver fidelity after \(2t\) physical walk steps as \(\mathcal F_N(2t)=\sin^4(\omega t/2)\), \(t\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\). Exact perfect state transfer at an integer walk time occurs if and only if \(N\in\{2,4,8\}\). The first exact transfer times are respectively \(2,4,6\) physical steps. For every other integer \(N\ge2\), \(\omega/\pi\) is irrational, so exact perfect transfer never occurs, but the irrational rotation \(t\omega\bmod 2\pi\) is dense and the same walk has pretty-good state transfer: for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is an integer \(t\) with \(\mathcal F_N(2t)>1-\varepsilon\). Thus the star model has a complete arithmetic dichotomy: three finite sizes have genuine discrete-time perfect transfer, while every other size has arbitrarily high fidelity but no exact unit-fidelity integer-time event.

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the proof; finite matrix replay is supplementary
integrity.novelty_scope: Exact integer-time exceptional-size classification and perfect-versus-pretty-good dichotomy for the source's marked coined star walk.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: The invariant subspace, eigenphase, and fidelity formula are credited to Štefaňák--Skoupý; general later pretty-good-transfer theory is credited to Chan--Zhan.

scientific_limitations: The theorem applies only to the marked coined star walk and source coin convention.
It gives a qualitative pretty-good transfer result, not an optimized error-versus-time bound.
It does not classify the complete-graph-with-loops or Szegedy models in the same source.
A later general discrete-time pretty-good-transfer theory may imply the result after a model identification not located explicitly in the inspected sources.
title: Exact versus pretty-good transfer in the marked coined walk on a star
